correctness.rationale: Adams--Shukla--Singh Lemma 2.2 identifies the scale-two intrinsic vertex-centered Čech nerve with the closed neighborhood simplex union. Distinct closed neighborhoods intersect in ≤2 vertices, making all 3-plus faces uniquely sourced. First collapse neighbor subsets size≥3; then remove each chord with unique common neighbor paired with its sole residual triangle. Remaining graph plus tetrahedral boundary per square is exact. One triangulated disk per square yields Q(G); second disk attaches along already filled square loop and contributes S². Torus C_m×C_n m,n≥5 is a cellular T² with mn squares, producing H1=Z² and H2=Z^{mn+1}, and nonzero torus cup product. The proof is for all admissible graphs, not finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: No other scales, equivariant splitting, K2,3 graphs; relies on established graph Čech closed-neighborhood identification.
